outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: The agent focusing on links only (has:link) rather than also running a separate has:file pass would be a minor gap if it still delivered a strong set of recent resources; also minor would be not hitting exactly 20 if fewer were available/visible and the agent explained that.

Critical issues: (1) The agent did not deliver the primary deliverable at all—no list of resources/messages was reported, let alone up to 20. (2) Therefore it also failed deduplication, failed to provide the required fields (title/filename, type, URL/domain, channel, sharer, timestamp, purpose), and failed to group results into documentation/source code/issue tracking/events/media/other. (3) The agent violated a hard constraint by opening an external link (“Limits”), navigating off Slack to an Auth0 page (daytonaio.us.auth0.com). Even aside from this violation, the outcome is still a failure because the user receives none of the requested extracted results.

Evidence: Screenshots/DOM states show Slack global search configured as `has:link` with Sort: Newest and 74 results (page 1 of 4), and visible result items include channel/context, sharer names, timestamps, at least one filename (image.png), and at least one visible domain/URL in message text. So the agent had accessible in-Slack information it could have compiled without opening any external links. The agent’s final output instead reports being blocked at Auth0 and provides no extracted resource entries. From an average user perspective, the task is not completed because the requested structured inventory is missing.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted a workspace-wide, most-recent-first inventory (up to 20 items) of shared resources (links or files) found via Slack global search filters, deduplicated and reported with specific per-item metadata (title/filename, type, URL/domain if visible, channel/DM, sharer, timestamp, and stated purpose), grouped into the requested categories. A reasonable user would be flexible about whether results come from link-filter or file-filter (either is fine) and minor formatting, but not flexible about missing the actual list of resources and required fields.
